description: Memory tools test case 1. Tests that agents can retrieve information from memory and inbox emails to perform complex email tasks. Session 1: 5 memory setup queries. Session 2: 5 emails inserted into inbox. Session 3: 5 reply/forward/send email queries requiring both memory and email information.

steps.user_message: Note that I studied for 3 hours on Monday, 4 hours on Tuesday, and 2.5 hours on Wednesday for my exam.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should acknowledge and save: I studied for 3 hours on Monday, 4 hours on Tuesday, and 2.5 hours on Wednesday for my exam
steps.agent_response:
Got it — you studied 3 hours on Monday, 4 hours on Tuesday, and 2.5 hours on Wednesday (total 9.5 hours). What would you like me to do with this info?

Options I can do for you:
- Draft or send an email reporting this (to a professor, tutor, study group, or yourself). I can send immediately or save as a draft.
- Save it as a draft note (I can create an email to yourself with the details).
- Create a short progress message you can copy elsewhere.

If you want an email, pick one of these templates or tell me how to change them and who to send to:

1) Formal to professor
Subject: Study hours logged for exam preparation
Body:
Hello Professor [Last name],
I wanted to update you on my exam preparation. I studied 3.0 hours on Monday, 4.0 hours on Tuesday, and 2.5 hours on Wednesday — a total of 9.5 hours. Please let me know if you have any recommendations for focusing the remainder of my study time.
Thank you,
[Your name]

2) Casual to study partner
Subject: Study update — 9.5 hours this week
Body:
Hey [Name],
Quick update: I put in 3 hrs (Mon), 4 hrs (Tue), and 2.5 hrs (Wed) — 9.5 hrs total so far. How are you doing? Want to plan a review session?
— [Your name]

3) Note-to-self (draft)
Subject: Exam study log — [dates]
Body:
Study log:
- Monday: 3.0 hours
- Tuesday: 4.0 hours
- Wednesday: 2.5 hours
Total: 9.5 hours

Tell me which action and template you want (send or save as draft), who the recipient is (email address or “myself”), and any personalization (names, sign-off). I’ll take care of it.

- The information can be phrased naturally, but all the key details must be present and accurate

- If the email is missing the specific details or contains incorrect numbers/dates/names, the validation MUST FAIL
- Partial matches or vague references are NOT sufficient - the exact information must be clearly present
